The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning).
parameters.name: anthropic-version

schema.description:
The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning).

parameters.description: The maximum number of user profiles to return, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
The cursor for the page to return, taken from `next_page` in a previous response.

Leave it out to get the first page.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: The sort direction, applied to the field that `order_by` selects. Defaults to `desc`.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: The field to sort user profiles by, in the direction that `order` sets. Defaults to `created_at`.
parameters.name: order_by

parameters.description: Return only the user profiles whose `enforcement_status` is one of these values: `unrestricted`, `pending`, `restricted` or `banned`. Repeat the parameter to match any of several. With it set, a page may hold fewer than `limit` profiles, or none, and still carry a `next_page`: the service examines a bounded number of profiles per request, and only a null `next_page` means the listing is complete. Rejected with `invalid_request_error` under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers. Fails with `overloaded_error` when a profile's enforcement actions cannot be read for the moment.
parameters.name: enforcement_status[]

parameters.description:
Optional header to select the Workspace for this request. The value is a Workspace ID (for example, `wrkspc_011CZkZaBF1tNoB5wlCeusgy`).

Only needed for credentials that can act on more than one Workspace. A credential that belongs to a specific Workspace may omit it; if sent, it must match that Workspace.
parameters.name: anthropic-workspace-id

400.description: Invalid argument - The client specified an invalid argument

401.description: Unauthenticated - The request does not have valid authentication credentials

403.description: Permission denied - The caller does not have permission to execute the specified operation

404.description: Not found - Some requested entity was not found

408.description: Deadline exceeded - The deadline expired before the operation could complete

409.description: Aborted - The operation was aborted due to concurrency issue

412.description: Failed precondition - Operation was rejected because the system is not in required state

413.description: Out of range - Operation was attempted past the valid range

429.description: Resource exhausted - Some resource has been exhausted (rate limiting)

431.description: Request header fields too large - Request metadata was too large

499.description: Cancelled - The operation was cancelled by the client

501.description: Unimplemented - The operation is not implemented or supported

503.description: Unavailable - The service is currently unavailable

504.description: Deadline exceeded - Upstream service did not respond in time

UserProfileListOrder.description: The direction that a list of user profiles is sorted in.

UserProfileListOrderBy.description: Sort field for listing user profiles: `created_at` (default) or `name` (case-insensitive; profiles without a name sort last).

UserProfileEnforcementStatus.description: Anthropic's enforcement status of this profile: `unrestricted`, `pending`, `restricted` or `banned`. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `restricted`.

ListUserProfilesResponse.description: A page of user profiles, sorted by the request's `order_by` and `order`.

next_page.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` when there are no more results.

UserProfile.description:
A record of an entity that the platform serves through the API, such as an end-user of the platform's product or a company that the platform resells Claude access to.

A Messages, Message Batches or token counting request can send a profile's `id` in the `anthropic-user-profile-id` header to attribute the request to that entity.

access_type.description: How the platform uses the API for this entity: `application` (default) or `passthrough`. Absent under the legacy `user-profiles-2026-03-24` beta header.

created_at.description: When this user profile was created, in RFC 3339 format.

enforcement_actions.description: The enforcement actions open on this profile; empty when none is open. Absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers.

enforcement_status.description: Anthropic's enforcement status of this profile, from its open enforcement actions and any identity check under review, by the first rule that applies: `banned` while any open action is a `ban`; `pending` while a restriction that an identity check can clear is open, the end user has submitted that check, Anthropic's review of it has not ended, and no open action's `reason` is `account_compromise`; `restricted` while any action is open; `unrestricted` while none is. Absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers.

external_user_details.description: Details about the entity this profile represents, as the platform states them; not verified by Anthropic. Every field is present, `null` until the platform supplies a value. Absent under the legacy `user-profiles-2026-03-24` and `user-profiles-2026-08-18` beta headers, which serve `reference_id` as the top-level `external_id` and, under `user-profiles-2026-08-18`, `onboarded_at` as `external_user_onboarded_at`.

id.description: Unique identifier for this user profile, prefixed `uprof_`.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata. Maximum 16 pairs, keys up to 64 chars, values up to 512 chars.

name.description: Real-world name of the entity this profile represents (company or individual). For a company the platform resells Claude access to (`access_type` `passthrough`) this is that company's name. `null` until the platform supplies one.

programs.description: The profile's standing in each Anthropic program, such as the Cyber Verification Program. Present when the request sends no user-profiles beta header; absent under the `user-profiles-2026-09-04` and earlier beta headers, which serve `trust_grants` instead.

updated_at.description: When this user profile was last modified, in RFC 3339 format. It normally also updates shortly after Anthropic gives the profile an approval or withdraws one. Other changes to the statuses that Anthropic reports do not always update it, so read the status itself rather than watching this timestamp.

UserProfileAccessType.description: How the platform uses the API on behalf of the entity this profile represents. `application`: the platform sells a product that uses the API behind the scenes, and the profile represents an individual end-user of that product. `passthrough`: the platform resells raw inference, and the profile identifies the resold-to company.

UserProfileEnforcementAction.description: A limit Anthropic has placed on the entity this profile represents and not yet resolved, discriminated by `type`: `restriction` or `ban`. More types may be added; read a `type` you do not recognize as `restriction`.

UserProfileExternalUserDetails.description: Details about the entity this profile represents, as the platform states them. Anthropic does not verify them. Every field is present, `null` until the platform supplies a value.

account_status.description: The status of the entity's account on the platform: `active`, `suspended` or `blocked`. `null` until the platform supplies one.

country.description: The country the platform associates with the entity, as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. `null` until the platform supplies one.

email_hash.description: The platform-computed hash of the entity's email address. `null` until the platform supplies one.

entity_type.description: What kind of entity the profile represents: `individual`, `business`, `non_profit` or `government`. `null` until the platform supplies one.

name_hash.description: The platform-computed hash of the entity's name. `null` until the platform supplies one.

onboarded_at.description: When the entity opened its account with the platform, as stated by the platform, in RFC 3339 format (UTC). `null` until the platform supplies one.

reference_id.description: The platform's own reference for the entity. `null` until the platform supplies one.

UserProfilePrograms.description: A user profile's standing in each program. A program is a set of capabilities or exemptions that Anthropic approves for the entity the profile represents. A program reads `null` when the profile has no status in it, when the caller's organization is not entitled to read programs, or when the response does not report that program. Retrieving the profile reports every program. Anthropic may add programs; ignore a key you do not recognize.

cyber.description: The profile's standing in the Cyber Verification Program. `null` when the profile has no status in it. Only retrieving the profile gives the full answer: a list or update response can show `null`, or a status other than `active`, for a profile that reads `active` when retrieved.

efs.description: The profile's standing in Enterprise Frontier Safeguards. `null` unless the platform's attestation for the program is in place on this profile, or the entity it represents has applied to the program. A list of user profiles does not report this program: there it reads `null` for every profile, so retrieve the profile to read it.

UserProfileEnforcementActionRestriction.description: Anthropic has limited how it serves the end user until the action is resolved. The end user may still be served in part.

action.description: The next step on the action: `verify` or `null`. `verify`: the end user can clear it now by passing an identity check. `null`: there is nothing the end user can do now to clear it, including while Anthropic reviews an identity check the end user submitted.

expires_at.description: When the action ends on its own, in RFC 3339 format; it stops showing once this time has passed. `null` when it has no end date, and always `null` when `reason` is `account_compromise`.

id.description: The action's ID (`enac_...`), stable while the action is open.

opened_at.description: When Anthropic opened the action, in RFC 3339 format.

reason.description: Why Anthropic placed the limit: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionBan.description: Anthropic has stopped serving the end user where the ban applies and does not plan to serve them there again.

action.description: Always `null`: the end user cannot clear a ban.

expires_at.description: Always `null`: a ban has no end date.

id.description: The action's ID (`enac_...`), stable while the action is open.

opened_at.description: When Anthropic opened the action, in RFC 3339 format.

reason.description: Why Anthropic placed the limit: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`.

UserProfileExternalUserAccountStatus.description: The status of the entity's account on the platform, as the platform states it: `active`; `suspended`, when the platform has restricted the account and may restore it; or `blocked`, when the platform has barred it. It records the platform's decision only. The statuses that Anthropic itself reports for the profile, such as its status in a program, are Anthropic's decisions and do not change with it.

UserProfileExternalUserEntityType.description: What kind of entity the profile represents, as the platform states it: `individual`, `business`, `non_profit` or `government`.

UserProfileCyberProgram.description: A user profile's standing in the Cyber Verification Program, which relaxes cyber safeguards for requests that name the profile.

requirements.description: What a request that names the profile must allow to get the relaxed safeguards of every `active` tier. `null` when no tier is `active`, and wherever `tiers` is `{}`.

status.description: `active` when at least one tier is `active`, or when the profile has the program's access to earlier models. That access is not a tier: a profile that has it alone reads `active` with every tier `inactive`, or with `tiers` `{}` on a response that does not report tiers. When nothing is `active`, `pending` means that an application or enrollment is under review, or that what Anthropic approved does not yet apply to this profile, and `rejected` means that the application or enrollment was declined.

tiers.description: The program's tiers, keyed by tier: `a` (Specialized Access), `b` (Red Team Access) and `c` (Defense Access). A response reports either every tier or none. When it reports them, as retrieving the profile normally does, every tier has a key, whether or not it applies to the profile. When it does not, as in the list of user profiles, `tiers` is `{}`, which does not mean that the tiers are inactive. No tier implies another, so read the tier you need. Anthropic may add tiers; ignore a key you do not recognize.

UserProfileEfsProgram.description: A user profile's standing in Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a program under which Anthropic approves the entity the profile represents and may approve any of the program's features.

features.description: The program's features, keyed by feature: `data_retention_exemption` (use of models that normally require data retention, without the data being retained), `cmek` (customer-managed encryption keys) and `storage` (customer-owned storage). Every feature that the caller's organization may read has a key, whether or not it is approved; a missing key does not mean that the feature is inactive. Anthropic may add features; ignore a key you do not recognize.

status.description: Anthropic's decision on the entity the profile represents: `pending` while it is awaited, `active` once Anthropic has approved the entity for the program, or `rejected` once Anthropic has declined or has removed the entity from the program. `active` does not mean that any one feature is approved: read the feature you need in `features`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionNextStep.description: The next step on this enforcement action: `verify` means the end user can clear the action by passing an identity check. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `null`.

UserProfileEnforcementActionReason.description: Why Anthropic placed this enforcement action: `unsupported_region`, `fraud_or_abuse`, `high_harm`, `usage_policy_violation`, `account_compromise` or `unspecified`. More values may be added; read a value you do not recognize as `unspecified`.

UserProfileCyberRequirements.description: What a request that names the profile must allow to get the relaxed safeguards of the profile's `active` tiers. A field reads `true` when at least one of those tiers has the requirement and Anthropic has not waived it on that tier for the profile. A request that does not meet a requirement is still served, without the relaxed safeguards of the tiers that have it. The values differ between profiles and can change, so read them rather than assuming them.

data_retention.description: Whether Anthropic must be able to retain the request's inference data.

human_review.description: Whether Anthropic personnel must be allowed to review the data retained from the request.

UserProfileProgramStatus.description: A user profile's status in a program. Each program's `status` field says what the values mean there.

UserProfileCyberTier.description: One tier of the Cyber Verification Program.

status.description: `active` when the tier applies to the profile, otherwise `inactive`. The response does not say why a tier is `inactive`: it can be in review, declined, withdrawn, never applied for, or approved but not applied to this profile.

UserProfileEfsFeature.description: One feature of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.

status.description: `active` when Anthropic has approved the entity the profile represents to use the feature, otherwise `inactive`. `active` does not mean that the feature is set up or switched on, which is a separate step.
